Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0039", "row_sha256": "f7921deb5948babaa094631b336b4f4398f216f6a267798b86cb7d5bbc6f84b7", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey can you put together the public timetable notice for the week at willow quay baths in alderwick, monday 14 october through sunday 20 october 2024. it should be a notice people can actually use to decide when to come, not a story about the pool and not the finished timetable being sent to me as a list of background facts. make it clear this is the weekly timetable and give the dates somewhere near the beginning. it needs to be prepared for Soraya, not Orson. i mean the copy is for Soraya, not Orson, so please use that recipient instruction clearly and don't turn it into a general announcement to both of them.

The building opens monday to friday from 6:30 am until 9 pm, on saturday 8 am to 6 pm and sunday 8 am to 4 pm. Those are the building hours, they aren't a promise that every pool or activity is available for all those hours. Main pool times are the useful bit. monday wednesday friday lane swimming 6:30-8, public swim 8-10, lessons 10-noon, lane swimming noon-2, club booking 2-4, family swim 4-6, lane swimming 6-8. Tuesday has lanes 6:30-8, public swim 8-10, lessons 10-noon, public swim noon-2, school booking 2-4, family swim 4-6, and adult swim 6-9. Thursday is mostly like tuesday after the morning, but not right at opening because maintenance people are checking the system. We don't want people thinking they can swim then. The main pool is unavailable until 8:15 am on thursday, then public swim 8:15-10, lessons 10-noon, public swim noon-2, school booking 2-4, family swim 4-6, adult swim 6-9. Say Thursday morning has the later opening for the pool, but don't imply the whole building opens later, the desk is open from 6:30 as usual.

There is a quote from Marnie, the pool supervisor, that could fit in the note if it's useful, it is exactly “We are checking the water system before the first session.” maybe don't use the quote as if she has guaranteed anything about what the checks will find; it is just her explanation of why the pool starts later that morning. No need to invent a result, she hasn't said what they find. The shallow teaching pool is open for parent-and-toddler sessions monday and wednesday 9-10 am and saturday 9-10 am. Booking is needed for those and the desk takes bookings in person or by phone, number 01632 441870. The teaching pool is not open swimming at other times in this timetable, it is used for lessons, so don't label it free swim or say anyone can drop in. Saturday in the main pool is lane swimming 8-10, lessons 10-noon, public swim noon-3, then family swim 3-5. Sunday main pool is public swim 8-11, lessons 11-1, family swim 1-3. Nothing is listed in either pool after those sunday activities, even though the building closes at 4, so don't fill the gap with a session.

Can you put the activities in a form people can scan quickly, probably with headings and maybe a numbered section where it makes sense. Need distinguish lanes from public swim, family swim, adult swim, school booking, club booking and lessons. Club and school times are not public access; make that explicit in a brief practical way. The three kinds of swimming are not interchangeable, and family swim is for families, not another name for public swim. Don't make up age limits or say what equipment people need. The lessons are scheduled but we haven't supplied lesson levels or ages, so don't invent those. Don't change the named activity or move any time to make the week look more even. A clear day-by-day arrangement is likely easiest, with the repeated monday wednesday friday pattern stated together if that stays easy to read. For tuesday and thursday, make the difference obvious, especially the later thursday main-pool start.

People need to know the lobby and changing area have step-free access, and the ramp entrance is on the car park side, not the street side. There are six accessible parking spaces at the car park entrance. The pool lift is available by asking the duty lifeguard; don't make it sound like it is automatically in use or that we know someone has requested it. The front desk is open the full building hours and takes payment for public swim and family swim, but the parent-and-toddler places are booked separately as above. No prices were agreed so just don't put in prices. We take card and cash at the desk. If mentioning anything about how to ask questions, say the desk can help with the week schedule. Don't invent an email, website, or social media contact.

Maybe use the ordinary quote from Marnie but keep her words exactly, and say she is the pool supervisor. There is also a small note that the café counter is open weekdays 8 am to 2 pm and saturday 9 am to 1 pm, closed sunday. It is not part of pool access and don't suggest someone can sit in the café during a swim session without paying or anything. Put that detail near the end as its own useful note rather than mixing it into swim slots. At the end mention that times are for this date range only; we don't have any later-week changes to announce. Don't add weather language, admission prices, a broad promotional slogan, or a claim that the maintenance check is done. Keep it friendly and direct. Make the notice complete with all the times, dates, contact number, access information and the distinct café hours, and no made-up sessions.", "output": "Prepare a clear, friendly public timetable notice for Willow Quay Baths in Alderwick, for Monday 14 October through Sunday 20 October 2024. The notice is for Soraya, not Orson. Make the date range clear near the beginning, and organize the information so visitors can quickly find the session and facility hours they need. Do not present a session as available outside its listed time.

The building is open Monday to Friday, 6:30 am–9 pm; Saturday, 8 am–6 pm; and Sunday, 8 am–4 pm. Distinguish these building hours from the hours of each pool and activity. Use a clear day-by-day layout. You may group Monday, Wednesday and Friday together if the repeated schedule remains easy to scan. Keep the named activities and times as supplied, and distinguish lane swimming, public swim, family swim, adult swim, lessons, school bookings and club bookings. School and club bookings are not open to the public.

1. Main pool schedule
- Monday, Wednesday and Friday: lane swimming 6:30–8 am; public swim 8–10 am; lessons 10 am–noon; lane swimming noon–2 pm; club booking 2–4 pm; family swim 4–6 pm; lane swimming 6–8 pm.
- Tuesday: lane swimming 6:30–8 am; public swim 8–10 am; lessons 10 am–noon; public swim noon–2 pm; school booking 2–4 pm; family swim 4–6 pm; adult swim 6–9 pm.
- Thursday: the building and desk open at 6:30 am as usual, but the main pool is unavailable until 8:15 am. Public swim runs 8:15–10 am; lessons 10 am–noon; public swim noon–2 pm; school booking 2–4 pm; family swim 4–6 pm; adult swim 6–9 pm. Make the later Thursday pool opening clear without suggesting that the whole building opens late.
- Saturday: lane swimming 8–10 am; lessons 10 am–noon; public swim noon–3 pm; family swim 3–5 pm.
- Sunday: public swim 8–11 am; lessons 11 am–1 pm; family swim 1–3 pm. Do not add a session after 3 pm, even though the building remains open until 4 pm.

2. Teaching pool and bookings
The shallow teaching pool has parent-and-toddler sessions Monday and Wednesday, 9–10 am, and Saturday, 9–10 am. These sessions require booking. Visitors can book in person at the desk or by phone on 01632 441870. At other times in this timetable, the teaching pool is used for lessons; it is not open swimming. Do not describe it as a drop-in or free-swim option. Lesson ages and levels have not been supplied, so do not add them.

Include a short explanation for the later start at the main pool on Thursday. Marnie, the pool supervisor, said: “We are checking the water system before the first session.” Keep the quotation exactly as written and do not imply that the check has produced a result.

3. Visitor information
The lobby and changing area have step-free access. The ramp entrance is on the car park side, not the street side. There are six accessible parking spaces at the car park entrance. The pool lift is available by asking the duty lifeguard; do not suggest that it is automatically in use or that anyone has requested it. The front desk is open throughout the building’s stated hours and can help with the week’s schedule. It takes card and cash, and handles payment for public swim and family swim. Parent-and-toddler sessions are booked separately as noted above. No prices have been supplied, so do not include any.

In a distinct note near the end, list the café counter hours: weekdays, 8 am–2 pm; Saturday, 9 am–1 pm; closed Sunday. Keep the café information separate from pool access and session times.

End by making clear that the timetable applies only to 14–20 October. No later-week changes have been announced. Keep the notice direct and practical. Include all supplied times, the booking phone number, access information and café hours. Do not add sessions, prices, contact details, age limits, equipment advice, promotional claims, weather language or a claim that the Thursday maintenance check is complete."}]
